title: admin-web TOTP 2FA is enforced only in the browser login page — no server-side AAL check exists anywhere, so the publicly-leaked admin password still opens the entire ops/finance/KYC surface
evidence: Enforcement lives entirely in the client: apps/admin-web/src/app/login/page.tsx:37-59 calls supabase.auth.mfa.getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel() and only decides whether to router.replace('/') or render a code field. apps/admin-web/src/lib/mfa.ts:49-61 (`mfaGate`) even documents the deferral: "The database is the real authority on what an aal1 session may do; this gate is a prompt, not a permission." But the database never checks it — `grep -rn "aal" supabase/migrations/*.sql supabase/functions/` returns ZERO hits; the only two occurrences of the string in the whole repo are the two client files above. Every admin RPC gates on role alone, e.g. `coalesce(public.auth_role()::text,'') <> 'admin'` in 20260730162600_p07_governance_hardening.sql:190 (admin_update_restaurant), 184_marketplace_integrity_and_food_safety.sql:160, 185_brand_gate_report.sql:38, 182_fx_rates.sql:211 (admin_set_fx_rate). The `authenticated`-granted admin RPC set includes admin_set_commission, admin_issue_credit / issue_credit, review_kyc_document, approve_restaurant, admin_grant_cod_override, admin_set_fx_rate, admin_assign_merchant_vertical, set_vertical_launch_stage. admin-web also has NO middleware.ts and no server route guard — apps/admin-web/src/app/OpsShell.tsx:63-79 reads only `users.role`, never assurance level. Context making this live rather than theoretical: docs/GO-LIVE.md:108-117 records that the `admin`-role dashboard password was printed in plaintext in this PUBLIC repo until 2026-07-30 (git history retains the blob), and the "Rotate the … password" item is still an UNCHECKED box (☐) at HEAD.
impact: An attacker holding the leaked password never touches admin.sharmeats.online. They POST to /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password with the public anon key, receive an aal1 JWT, and call the admin RPCs directly against PostgREST. TOTP enrolment changes nothing on that path: Supabase issues the aal1 session regardless of a verified factor. That reaches commission rates, credit issuance (real money out), KYC approval, FX rates, vertical launch stage and dispatch. The mitigation shipped in eab5449 for exactly this incident provides zero protection against the incident's own threat model, while docs/GO-LIVE.md:129-132 presents it to the operator as protection.
fix_sketch: Make assurance level a database fact, not a screen. Add `public.auth_aal()` reading `(auth.jwt() ->> 'aal')` and require `= 'aal2'` inside every admin-gated RPC (fail-closed with coalesce, per house rule 4) — cheapest as one shared `public.require_admin()` helper that both role-checks and aal-checks, then swap the ~17 inline `auth_role() <> 'admin'` guards to call it. Gate on a platform_settings flag so the single admin cannot lock themselves out before enrolling. Independently: complete the GO-LIVE.md:113 rotation checkbox and audit Supabase auth logs back to 2026-06-06 as that doc already instructs.

title: Mig 201 fresh-ping dispatch filter + driver app that never pings while idle = fleet goes invisible to auto-dispatch after 5 idle minutes
evidence: supabase/migrations/201_dispatch_requires_fresh_ping.sql:56-64 — nearest_drivers now requires coalesce(last_ping_at,'-infinity') > now() - 300s (platform_settings dispatch_max_ping_age_seconds). But last_ping_at is only refreshed by driver_ping, and the driver app calls it in exactly four places: on going online (apps/driver/app/home.tsx:156), on going offline (home.tsx:162), on AppState foreground transition (home.tsx:109-120), and during the background location task which runs ONLY while an active delivery is streaming (apps/driver/src/location.ts:10-12 'we only stream while on an ACTIVE delivery'; backgroundLocationTask.ts handleLocationBatch returns early unless ACTIVE_ORDER_STORAGE_KEY is set). grep across apps/driver finds no setInterval/heartbeat ping (only UI countdown timers in DeliveryCountdown.tsx/OfferCard.tsx). So an online driver waiting between jobs — app backgrounded or even open but untouched for 5 minutes — stops satisfying the filter and is silently excluded from every nearest_drivers call in auto_assign_order (189_dispatch_pickup_centered.sql:53-58).
impact: Auto-dispatch can only reach drivers who toggled online, foregrounded the app, or finished a delivery within the last 5 minutes. In the common launch-scale scenario (small fleet, drivers waiting with phones pocketed), dispatch_sweep finds zero candidates for every new order: no offer row is created, so no new_offer push, no realtime offer, nothing wakes the drivers — a deadlock where the order waits for a ping and the driver waits for a push. Orders sit unassigned until dispatch_watchdog (default 10 min, alert-cooldown 60 min per mig 119) pages ops for manual assignment. Applied 2026-07-31 (newest migration), so this is a live regression, not a deferred item — mig 201 fixed dead seed phones but assumed idle pings exist; the client never made that true.
fix_sketch: Either (a) add an idle heartbeat in the driver app: while status==='online' and not streaming, call pingOnce() on a ~60-120s timer plus a silent background-fetch task for backgrounded phones; or (b) server-side, treat last_ping_at staleness as a soft signal when the driver has push tokens registered (e.g. still offer but prefer fresh-ping drivers), or raise dispatch_max_ping_age_seconds until (a) ships. Ship (a) as an OTA (JS-only) and keep 300s.

title: Mig 201 fresh-ping dispatch gate has no client counterpart: idle-online drivers become undispatchable 300s after their last app interaction, stranding orders on auto-dispatch
evidence: supabase/migrations/201_dispatch_requires_fresh_ping.sql:56-64 — nearest_drivers now requires coalesce(d.last_ping_at,'-infinity') > now() - dispatch_max_ping_age_seconds (default 300s, seeded at :39-41). But the driver app only writes last_ping_at (via driver_ping RPC) at three moments: (1) toggling online (apps/driver/app/home.tsx:156), (2) an AppState background→active transition (home.tsx:109-120), (3) during an ACTIVE delivery via the background location task — apps/driver/src/location.ts:10-12 states 'we only stream while on an ACTIVE delivery', and startStreaming is called only from app/job/[id].tsx:79,110. There is no periodic heartbeat while idle-online: grep for setInterval across apps/driver hits only OfferCard/DeliveryCountdown UI timers. Even a driver with the app OPEN on the home screen stops pinging 15s after going online (driver_ping throttle, mig 032). Mig 201 shipped 2026-07-31 in commit 9f71fc0 with zero apps/driver changes (git show --stat 9f71fc0).
impact: Any driver waiting for work with phone locked or app backgrounded >5 min — the normal state of an idle fleet — silently disappears from every nearest_drivers call. dispatch_sweep then finds no candidates for every new order, so auto-dispatch is effectively dark whenever the fleet is idle; each order waits ~10 min for the dispatch_watchdog alert (mig 133) and then needs manual assign_driver. In a thin launch fleet this converts essentially every quiet-hour order into a stranded-then-manual order. (The migration correctly fixes the 3,429-lap stale-seed-driver loop; the regression is that it also excludes genuinely-available drivers.)
fix_sketch: Ship a pairing client change before (or with) enabling the 300s threshold: a foreground interval ping while online (e.g. every 60-120s from home.tsx) plus a background heartbeat while online (background fetch task, or extend the location task to idle-online with coarse accuracy), and/or have the expo-push receipt path refresh last_ping_at. Interim ops mitigation: raise platform_settings.dispatch_max_ping_age_seconds to a value matched to real app-interaction cadence, and treat a recent successful push receipt as evidence of a listening phone.

title: Rejected/cancelled orders permanently consume one-time minted credit codes — no redemption release or wallet re-credit anywhere
evidence: place_order inserts promo_redemptions at placement (153_vertical_stage_enforcement.sql:334-339, 'on conflict (order_id) do nothing'); validate_promo enforces per_user_limit/max_uses by counting ALL promo_redemptions rows with no order-outcome filter (058_minted_promo_owner_binding.sql, per_user_limit block); redeem_credit debits customer_credit_balance at MINT time and creates a per_user_limit=1 code (122_referral_reward_crypto_fix.sql:75-122); grep across all 204 migrations finds no DELETE/void of promo_redemptions and no compensating issue_credit on any cancel/reject path (advance_order_status lineage and all files matching 'cancelled' contain none).
impact: A customer who applies a CR- (refund/SLA/goodwill credit), LOY-, or REF- code to an order that the merchant then rejects — a routine flow (out of stock, closed) — loses the full credit: balance was debited at mint, the code's single use is consumed by the dead order, and nothing re-credits. This silently destroys the exact compensation the app legally promises (SLA auto-credit, Consumer Protection Law 181/2018 exposure documented in PLATFORM-GAPS). Also burns per-user uses of public campaign codes on rejected orders.
fix_sketch: In advance_order_status (or an AFTER UPDATE trigger on the cancelled/rejected transition), delete or mark-void the order's promo_redemptions row so validate_promo's counts exclude it; for owner-bound CR- codes, additionally re-credit the wallet via a definer path (reason 'adjustment', idempotent per order) instead of resurrecting the code.

title: Credit-to-code conversion silently burns the remainder when the code's value exceeds the order subtotal
evidence: apps/customer/app/(tabs)/rewards.tsx:162 redeems the ENTIRE balance in one call (redeemCredit(creditEgp)); redeem_credit debits the full amount immediately (122_referral_reward_crypto_fix.sql:75-122); validate_promo caps the discount at subtotal — 'return greatest(0, least(v_discount, coalesce(p_subtotal,0)))' — and the delivery/service fees are not coverable (058_minted_promo_owner_binding.sql, final return); per_user_limit=1 consumes the code after that single partial use, and place_order books only v_discount (153:286,303).
impact: A customer holding e.g. 100 EGP of credit (typical SLA credit cap is 100, mig 135) who applies the minted code to an 80 EGP-subtotal order gets 80 off and irrecoverably loses 20 EGP — no warning in validate_promo, no residual code, no wallet return. Bounded per-customer money loss in the flow that fulfills the advertised compensation promise.
fix_sketch: Either (a) let the customer choose the redemption amount in the UI and warn when code value > basket subtotal, or (b) server-side: on redemption, write back the unused remainder to customer_credit_balance in the same place_order transaction (discount_egp is known there), or cap the mint at a chosen amount rather than full balance.

title: record_delivery_proof path check NULL-propagates: any suffix-less storage_path is accepted, letting a driver forge a dangling proof row and defeat the missing-proof ops report
evidence: supabase/migrations/194_proof_of_delivery.sql:240-245: `if p_storage_path is null or p_storage_path <> v_user::text || '/' || p_order_id::text || substring(p_storage_path from '-[0-9]+\.(?:jpg|jpeg|png|webp)$') then raise`. When the path does NOT end in `-<digits>.<ext>`, substring() returns NULL, string concatenation makes the whole right side NULL, `p_storage_path <> NULL` evaluates to NULL, and `false OR NULL` = NULL, which plpgsql treats as false — the exception is NOT raised and the INSERT at lines 250-252 proceeds with the arbitrary path. The migration's own comment (lines 237-239) says this check exists precisely so 'a driver could [not] index a path pointing at somebody else's prefix'. supabase/tests/194_proof_of_delivery.test.sql:296-312 only tests refusal with well-formed `-<epoch>.jpg` suffixes, so the bypass is untested. Violates the repo's own house rule 4 (fail closed on NULL) from CLAUDE.md.
impact: The assigned driver on an order at handoff can call record_delivery_proof with a junk path (e.g. 'x', '', 'other-uid/foo.png') and mint a delivery_proofs row with no bytes behind it. ops_deliveries_missing_proof (same migration, lines 296-298) treats ANY delivery_proofs row as proof, so the one control that polices photo-less leave_at_door/no_bell COD deliveries (the stated counterweight for not DB-gating the delivered transition, lines 10-18) is silently whitewashed — 'never arrived' COD disputes lose their evidence check. Secondary: junk rows pollute the unique storage_path evidence index.
fix_sketch: Make the comparison null-safe and fail closed: `v_suffix := substring(p_storage_path from '-[0-9]+\.(?:jpg|jpeg|png|webp)$'); if p_storage_path is null or v_suffix is null or p_storage_path <> v_user::text || '/' || p_order_id::text || v_suffix then raise ...` (or use IS DISTINCT FROM per house rule 4). Add a regression case with a suffix-less path to supabase/tests/194_proof_of_delivery.test.sql. Optionally backfill-audit existing delivery_proofs rows whose storage_path fails the shape.

title: Mig 200 fixed the driver_assigned push loop by routing three events into an outbox that has no dispatcher — those notifications are now never sent at all
evidence: supabase/migrations/200_driver_assigned_notification_loop.sql:60-96 replaces the direct net.http_post (mig 073) with public.enqueue_push() for driver_assigned (customer), order_ready_pickup (assigned driver) and low_rating (merchant staff). enqueue_push (172_enqueue_push.sql:93-113) only INSERTs a push_messages row with status='queued' — it performs no HTTP call. Nothing in the repo consumes queued push_messages: grep across supabase/functions/ and all 204 migrations shows the only readers are claim_push_retries (173, reads push_attempts, which are created only when the expo-push edge function is invoked directly) and the read-only inbox/receipt paths. expo-push/index.ts is invoked only by direct sender POSTs; expo-push-receipts only polls tickets. The program doc confirms the dispatcher is a NOT-YET-DONE rollout step: docs/implementation-program/03-notifications-and-crm.md:393-395 ('5. Migrate senders to enqueue. 6. Deploy dispatcher and receipt poller.') — mig 200 executed step 5 for one sender before step 6 exists. Mig 171's own parallel-run rule ('senders BOTH enqueue here and keep their existing direct send', 171_push_outbox.sql:46-48) was violated.
impact: Shipped 2026-07-31 (after the 07-24 audit — in scope). Customers are never told a driver is on the way; the assigned driver is never pinged that a ready order awaits pickup (food sits, deliveries slow); merchants never hear about low ratings. driver_assigned is in ESSENTIAL_EVENTS (expo-push/prefs.ts:36) precisely because missing it means cold food at an unanswered door. The queued rows also expire (30 min for driver_assigned) and never even surface in the mig 179 inbox (status stays 'queued', inbox filters to complete/partly_failed). Same trap will bite lifecycle marketing (migs 177/178) the day lifecycle_mode is flipped to 'live': enqueue-only, zero sends, ledger says sent.
fix_sketch: Ship the missing outbox dispatcher before anything else: a claim_queued_push_messages RPC (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, mirroring 173) + a pg_cron sweep that POSTs each claimed message to expo-push (or a new expo-push 'outbox' mode that accepts message ids), created in a numbered migration. Until it exists, an interim migration can restore the direct net.http_post for these three events guarded by a sent-marker (e.g. insert-or-skip on the existing idempotency key with status set terminally) so the 2026-07-31 loop does not return.

title: Push retry pipeline is dead code: claim_push_retries/settle_push_attempt have no caller, so retryable_failed attempts are never re-sent and the ATTEMPT_CAP dead letter is unreachable
evidence: supabase/migrations/173_push_retry_claim.sql:64-145 defines claim_push_retries; grep across the entire repo (edge functions, apps, all migrations) finds zero callers, and no cron.schedule in any migration invokes it (full cron.schedule inventory checked). No edge function can even send a claimed attempt: expo-push/index.ts's contract is event+recipients (index.ts:54-76), not attempt rows, and expo-push-receipts only calls getReceipts. Meanwhile both producers keep minting retryable work nothing consumes: expo-push marks 429/5xx/network failures retryable_failed with next_attempt_at (index.ts:337-355, 403-414; outbox.ts:258-261) and expo-push-receipts re-marks retryable receipts the same way (expo-push-receipts/index.ts:170-177 — comment 'The dispatcher picks this up'). docs/OPS-RUNBOOK.md:388-392 lists a 'Runs' schedule for every piece except claim_push_retries, which has none.
impact: A push batch lost to an Expo 429/5xx or a network blip is recorded but never retried — functionally the same silent permanent loss the whole Package 03 outbox (migs 171-175, deployed 2026-07-30) exists to fix, now with paperwork. Expo rate-limiting is exactly a volume behavior, so this bites hardest during the marketing-driven peaks this pre-scale audit is for. Rows churn retryable_failed until message expiry, then read as 'expired'; the documented dead-letter queue (error_code ATTEMPT_CAP) can never be reached, so operator dashboards built on it will always read clean.
fix_sketch: Build the Slice D dispatcher (same component as finding 1): cron-invoked edge function (or expo-push mode) that calls claim_push_retries(), sends each claimed token via the Expo API, and settles via settle_push_attempt(). Schedule it in a migration (every 1-2 min), not by hand in the dashboard.

title: Mig 200 routes driver_assigned / order_ready_pickup / low_rating into a push outbox that has NO dispatcher — these three notifications are now never sent at all
evidence: supabase/migrations/200_driver_assigned_notification_loop.sql:60-97 replaces the previous direct net.http_post sends (mig 073, proven working by the very incident the header describes) with enqueue_push-only calls. enqueue_push (172_enqueue_push.sql:93-112) inserts push_messages rows with status 'queued' and returns. Exhaustive search: the ONLY consumers of push_messages anywhere in the repo are the inbox/open RPCs (175_notification_open.sql:81, 179_notification_inbox.sql:92,142,213) and the edge functions' own bookkeeping (expo-push/outbox.ts, expo-push-receipts/index.ts:74) — nothing selects status='queued' rows to send them. claim_push_retries (173_push_retry_claim.sql:85-117) only claims push_attempts rows, which are created solely by the direct-send path (expo-push/outbox.ts recordAttempts), and requires push_token_id — fresh queued messages have zero attempts. No cron.schedule in any migration invokes a push dispatcher (full cron list grepped), and the verified prod deployed-function list (delete-account, expo-push, paymob-webhook, telegram-bot, expo-push-receipts) contains no dispatcher. Worse, the inbox RPC filters `m.status in ('complete','partly_failed')` (179_notification_inbox.sql:~152), so the forever-'queued' rows are invisible there too. Shipped 2026-07-31 (commit 9f71fc0), after the 07-24 audit — a regression, not a deferred item.
impact: Since 2026-07-31, customers are never told a driver is on the way (driver_assigned), drivers are never pinged that an order is ready for pickup when the app is backgrounded (order_ready_pickup — orders sit ready at the counter), and merchant staff never receive low-rating alerts. The messages expire silently (30 min / 1 h windows per mig 172) with no error, no inbox entry, and no alert; the fix for the infinite-push incident traded 'sends forever' for 'sends never'.
fix_sketch: Ship the missing consumer before anything else: (a) a dispatcher edge function + a claim_queued_push_messages RPC (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, same pattern as mig 173) that takes status='queued' rows, POSTs them to expo-push, and settles them; plus a pg_cron job for it and one for claim_push_retries. Interim hotfix: in notify_order_transition, keep enqueue_push for dedupe but net.http_post directly to expo-push ONLY when enqueue_push inserted a NEW row (compare returned id against a pre-existing lookup, or add an OUT flag), restoring delivery while keeping the once-per-order key.

title: public.users.locale is never written by any client and defaults to 'ar' — push copy is sent in Arabic to every customer regardless of chosen app language, making the 5-locale push layer dead in practice
evidence: expo-push localizes per recipient from public.users.locale (supabase/functions/expo-push/index.ts:263-276, copy.ts resolveCopy). But handle_new_user sets locale from signup metadata with `coalesce(...,'ar')` (124_signup_role_hint_lockdown.sql:59, same in 002/007), and the customer app calls sb.auth.signInAnonymously() with no metadata (apps/customer/src/data/supabase/auth.ts:149) and never passes locale on the phone-link upgrade (auth.ts:185). The in-app language picker only writes the zustand store + AsyncStorage (apps/customer/app/settings.tsx:155, app/onboarding.tsx:159 → src/store/session.ts:272-275); userRepoSupabase.update supports a locale patch (src/data/supabase/user.ts:50) but no call site ever passes it (repo-wide grep). The driver and restaurant apps likewise persist their new AR toggle to AsyncStorage only (apps/driver/src/i18n-context.tsx:60-68, apps/restaurant/src/localePersistence.ts). No migration or trigger writes users.locale after signup (grep across supabase/migrations).
impact: Every push in the paid flow — order status, payment_failed, order_rejected, driver offers, merchant new-order alerts — renders from a locale column frozen at 'ar' at signup. A Russian or English tourist who set the app to RU/EN gets Arabic lock-screen notifications; an English-speaking merchant staffer gets Arabic order alerts. The N4 i18n work (copy.ts, 29 events x 5 locales, per-locale Expo chunking) is effectively unreachable, and its comment 'guests fall back to en' is wrong — guests get a users row defaulted to 'ar'.
fix_sketch: Three small patches: (1) pass options.data.locale (device language) in signInAnonymously/signup; (2) in setLocale, when a session exists, also fire userRepo.update({ locale }) (fire-and-forget); (3) same one-line users update in the driver/restaurant AR toggles. Optionally backfill existing rows where locale='ar' is provably signup-default (e.g. from analytics locale context) or leave and let next app open sync it.

title: mark_cod_collected has no order-status gate: COD can be marked paid pre-delivery (or on a cancelled order) and the resulting paid+cancelled state is invisible to reconciliation
evidence: supabase/migrations/104_driver_cash_reconciliation.sql (latest definer, ~lines 150-220): checks only payment_method='cash_on_delivery', amount==total_egp, and actor (admin / assigned driver / self-delivery merchant staff) — v_order.status is never examined, so the RPC is callable at placed/accepted/preparing/picked_up and even on cancelled/rejected orders. The gate exists only in the driver app UI (apps/driver/src/jobs.ts:367-373; app/job/[id].tsx:509), violating the project's own 'authority lives in Postgres' rule. Downstream: admin/dispatcher may cancel any non-terminal order (033/latest 103 advance_order_status wildcard-cancel branch); settle_driver_period sums driver_earnings with NO order-status filter (supabase/migrations/105_payout_details_and_driver_settlements.sql:108-125); and mig 181's detector cannot see it — class 'cod_delivered_uncollected' filters o.status='delivered' (181_payment_reconciliation.sql:169-179) and class 'card_captured_but_cancelled' filters payment_method='card' (181:217-227).
impact: Assigned driver taps 'collect' early (or retries on a just-cancelled order), then the order is cancelled: orders stays payment_status='paid' on a cancelled COD order with no un-pay path, a driver_earnings row (fee+tip+bonus) flows into the next driver settlement for a delivery that never happened, and driver_cash_ledger records cash custody the driver may not hold. No sweep or reconciliation class ever flags it; each occurrence is a silent, manual-forensics accounting corruption on the launch payment rail.
fix_sketch: In mark_cod_collected require v_order.status in ('out_for_delivery','delivered') (admin override at most). Add a 'cod_paid_but_cancelled' mismatch class to payment_reconciliation_findings mirroring class h for cash orders (payment_status='paid' AND status in ('cancelled','rejected') AND payment_method='cash_on_delivery').

title: A genuinely LOST Paymob webhook leaves a captured charge with zero local trace — mig 181 reconciles late webhooks, not lost ones, and nothing ever polls Paymob
evidence: reconcile_stale_card_orders (033_card_payment_guards.sql:178-205) cancels a pending card order after 30 min regardless of provider state. If Paymob captured the charge but the webhook never arrives (all retries exhausted / endpoint down), payment_attempts stays status='ready' and orders stays payment_status='failed': every mig 181 detector class keys off a 'paid' row — class a needs payment_status='paid' (181:99-111), class b needs attempt status='paid' (181:114-126), class h needs payment_status='paid' (181:217-227). No code anywhere queries Paymob's transaction-inquiry API (the only outbound Paymob calls in the repo are paymob-create-intention/index.ts:207 and paymob-refund/index.ts:160); 181's design is explicitly DB-only ('this migration watches the money data itself').
impact: Dormant while card is dark, but once enabled: customer charged, order auto-cancelled, and no alert, report row, or record anywhere states that money moved — detection depends entirely on Paymob's webhook retry durability or a customer complaint. This is the one 'paid-but-webhook-lost' branch the new reconciliation package does not actually cover.
fix_sketch: Before enabling card, add a reconciler for attempts stuck at status='ready' whose order was cancelled/failed N minutes ago: either a cron-driven edge function that queries Paymob transaction inquiry by provider_order_id/intention_id (both already persisted by create-intention index.ts:277-289), or minimally a mismatch class 'checkout_expired_unverified' in 181 so an operator is told to verify those attempts in the Paymob dashboard.

title: Admin DispatchBoard realtime has no reconnect resync — events lost during any socket drop leave the ops board silently stale
evidence: apps/admin-web/src/app/DispatchBoard.tsx:60-84 — .subscribe() is called with NO status callback and there is no refetch anywhere after mount (initialOrders/initialDrivers are server-rendered once). Every other realtime consumer in the repo carries the [H-CUST2] fix: on SUBSCRIBED it refetches because "supabase-js rejoins the channel after a network drop but never replays events emitted during the outage" (apps/customer/src/data/supabase/orders.ts:298-313, apps/merchant-web/src/app/OrderQueue.tsx:102-118, apps/restaurant/src/orders.ts:317-324, apps/driver/src/jobs.ts:293-295). DispatchBoard is the only subscriber without it.
impact: The admin dispatch board is the manual-dispatch authority surface. After a laptop sleep / network blip, supabase-js silently rejoins but every order placed, assigned, or terminated during the outage is permanently missing or ghost-listed until a full page reload: a new platform order never appears in needsDispatch (order sits undispatched if dispatch_mode is manual), and a cancelled order stays on the board. There is no staleness indicator, so the operator has no way to know the board diverged. (The @20s auto-assign sweep and 5m watchdog bound the damage in auto mode, hence P1 not P0.)
fix_sketch: Mirror the existing pattern: .subscribe((status) => { if (status === 'SUBSCRIBED') { refetch active orders + active drivers and setOrders/setDrivers } }), reusing the same queries the server component runs for initialOrders/initialDrivers; optionally surface CHANNEL_ERROR/TIMED_OUT as a visible "reconnecting" banner.

title: record_delivery_proof path guard fails OPEN for paths that don't match the suffix regex — drivers can fabricate proof-of-delivery rows
evidence: supabase/migrations/194_proof_of_delivery.sql:239-245: `if p_storage_path is null or p_storage_path <> v_user::text || '/' || p_order_id::text || substring(p_storage_path from '-[0-9]+\.(?:jpg|jpeg|png|webp)$')`. When p_storage_path does not match the regex, substring() returns NULL, the `||` concatenation becomes NULL, `p_storage_path <> NULL` evaluates NULL, and the IF branch does not fire — the insert at :251 proceeds with the arbitrary path. This is the exact NULL-comparison fail-open the function's own comment (194:210-211) warns about for v_role. ops_deliveries_missing_proof (194:296-298) then excludes the order via `not exists (select 1 from delivery_proofs dp where dp.order_id = o.id)`, so the fabricated row blinds the detective control. supabase/tests/194_proof_of_delivery.test.sql:296-312 tests only wrong-prefix/wrong-order paths that DO match the regex; the non-matching case is untested.
impact: The assigned driver on any out_for_delivery/delivered order can call record_delivery_proof(order_id, 'garbage') and mint a delivery_proofs row pointing at a nonexistent object — no photo ever uploaded. Leave-at-door/COD deliveries that required photo evidence appear proofed, the ops missing-proof report (the stated counterweight to not gating the status transition) is silently defeated, and dispute/fraud evidence is forgeable by the party it is meant to check. Shipped post-2026-07-24 audit, live schema path.
fix_sketch: Fail closed on a non-matching suffix: compute `v_suffix := substring(p_storage_path from '-[0-9]+\.(?:jpg|jpeg|png|webp)$')` first and `raise INVALID_PROOF_PATH` when `v_suffix is null OR p_storage_path is distinct from v_user::text || '/' || p_order_id::text || v_suffix`. Add the non-matching-path case to 194's harness test.

title: private.delivery_encrypt/delivery_decrypt pin a search_path that excludes `extensions` while calling bare pgp_sym_encrypt/decrypt — every delivery-job creation will hard-fail on prod (same bug class mig 197 just fixed, missed these two)
evidence: supabase/migrations/193_delivery_job_model.sql:27-57: both functions set `search_path = private, public, pg_temp` and call unqualified `pgp_sym_encrypt(...)`/`pgp_sym_decrypt(...)` (:39, :56). 197_gen_random_bytes_search_path_fix.sql:8-14 proves ON THE LIVE DB (2026-07-30) that pgcrypto is installed in the `extensions` schema and is unresolvable under a pinned search_path that omits it (`to_regprocedure` NULL). 197 ALTERs only redeem_points, redeem_credit, reward_referrer_on_delivery and create_order_share — grep confirms no migration fixes delivery_encrypt/delivery_decrypt, and 193:433-441 shows create_delivery_job calls delivery_encrypt for every endpoint/parcel snapshot. No test exercises it: grep of supabase/tests/ finds zero references to delivery_encrypt or create_delivery_job.
impact: On production, the first create_delivery_job call raises 42883 'function pgp_sym_encrypt(text, text) does not exist' — the entire Package 08 delivery-jobs product cannot create a single job when the dark flag is opened. Latent today (delivery stage disabled, internal-only) and invisible to the local harness (a fresh Postgres replay of 001/002 puts pgcrypto in public, where the bare call resolves), i.e. exactly the tests-pass/prod-fails failure mode that stranded redeem_points for months (audit H-03).
fix_sketch: One-line migration mirroring 197: `alter function private.delivery_encrypt(text) set search_path = private, public, extensions, pg_temp;` and same for delivery_decrypt(bytea) (or schema-qualify as extensions.pgp_sym_encrypt). Add a plpgsql_check run over `private` (197's sweep covered only nspname='public', which is why these were missed).

title: assign_driver never validates or locks the order: dispatchers can create live offers on terminal orders, and it races auto_assign_order into two concurrent offers
evidence: supabase/migrations/150_cod_ceiling_enforcement.sql:41-90 (latest assign_driver) — the body checks role and driver eligibility but never SELECTs public.orders at all: no existence/status check, no FOR UPDATE. Contrast auto_assign_order (189_dispatch_pickup_centered.sql:27-30) which locks the order row and bails if status not in ('accepted','preparing','ready') or an offered/accepted assignment exists. driver_respond (030_driver_verified_gate.sql:80-99) accepts based solely on the assignment row being 'offered' — it never re-checks the order's status or assigned_driver_id.
impact: Two concrete holes. (1) Terminal orders: a dispatcher (fat-finger or stale admin-web screen) can assign a driver to a delivered/cancelled order; the driver accepts, is set on_job (030:99), and is never released — the mig 054/103 release only runs inside advance_order_status on a terminal transition, and terminal states have no outgoing transitions, so the driver is stranded out of the dispatch pool until they manually toggle offline/online. (2) Race: assign_driver holds no order lock, so interleaving with the 20s dispatch sweep can yield two simultaneous 'offered' assignments (auto to A, manual to B); both pass driver_respond's 'offered' check, both go on_job, two drivers arrive at the restaurant for one order.
fix_sketch: In assign_driver: `select * into v_order from public.orders where id=p_order_id for update;` raise if not found or status not in ('placed','accepted','preparing','ready'); the existing 'mark prior offered/accepted reassigned' then runs under the same lock ordering as auto_assign_order, closing the double-offer race. In driver_respond accept path, assert the parent order is non-terminal.

title: Manual reassignment of an accepted order strands the displaced driver 'on_job' forever (the mig-054 fleet-decay bug, alive on the dispatcher path)
evidence: supabase/migrations/150_cod_ceiling_enforcement.sql:82 — assign_driver marks the prior 'accepted' assignment 'reassigned' and repoints orders.assigned_driver_id to the new driver, but never resets the displaced driver's drivers.status. The ONLY on_job→online reset in the entire migration set is inside advance_order_status (grep "set status = 'online'" hits only 054:119 and 103:92), and that release is keyed to v_order.assigned_driver_id at terminal time — i.e. the NEW driver. nearest_drivers requires status='online' (201:56), so the displaced driver receives no further auto offers.
impact: Every time a dispatcher rescues an order by reassigning it away from a driver who had accepted (driver unreachable, bike broke down — exactly the situations where manual reassign is used), the old driver silently drops out of the dispatch pool for the rest of their shift. The driver app's toggle reads status !== 'offline' as online (documented in 054's header), so the driver sees 'online · receiving offers' while getting none. Fleet capacity decays one rescue at a time; invisible except as falling acceptance volume.
fix_sketch: In assign_driver (and any future reassignment path), before repointing: `update public.drivers set status='online' where id = (select assigned_driver_id from orders where id=p_order_id) and id <> p_driver_id and status='on_job';` — same guarded pattern as mig 054. Also reset when driver_respond marks an accepted assignment reassigned.

title: Scheduled orders are gated client-side only: place_order still stores arbitrary scheduled_for and every lifecycle sweep ignores it — a scheduled order is cooked and dispatched immediately
evidence: Latest place_order body (supabase/migrations/153_vertical_stage_enforcement.sql:145,306,320; mig 162 only re-comments it) accepts p_scheduled_for with zero validation (not even future-dated) and writes orders.scheduled_for verbatim. No lifecycle component reads it: auto_accept_sweep selects any status='placed' older than 180s (026_auto_accept.sql:82-91), dispatch_sweep dispatches any accepted/preparing/ready order (033_card_payment_guards.sql dispatch_sweep body), auto_advance_sweep likewise (039) — grep 'scheduled' across 025/026/033/039/060/189 returns nothing. The gate is purely in the client: apps/customer/app/checkout.tsx:144-145 nulls scheduledFor when EXPO_PUBLIC_SCHEDULED_ORDERS_ENABLED !== 'true' (false in apps/customer/eas.json:28; commit 8c5e28a 'gate scheduled orders until lifecycle is safe').
impact: Any pre-gate app build still in the field with the scheduling UI, or any authenticated user calling the RPC directly with p_scheduled_for, places an order that the kitchen auto-accepts within 3 minutes and dispatch delivers now — food for 'Saturday 19:00' arrives today, real money (COD) charged, near-certain refund/dispute. The DB boundary that the architecture doc says holds all authority does not enforce the one invariant the client gate exists for.
fix_sketch: Server-side, mirror the gate where authority lives: in place_order, `if p_scheduled_for is not null then raise exception 'SCHEDULED_ORDERS_DISABLED'` (or clamp to null) until the lifecycle work lands; when it does land, auto_accept_sweep/dispatch_sweep must add `and (o.scheduled_for is null or o.scheduled_for - lead_time < now())`.

title: dispatch_watchdog cannot see the two stuck-order shapes that actually occur: offer-churn loops and never-expiring manual offers (assigned_driver_id is non-null in both)
evidence: supabase/migrations/133_watchdog_placed_orders.sql — v_stuck counts only status in ('accepted','ready') AND assigned_driver_id IS NULL (lines ~40-45). But (a) during an offer-churn loop, auto_assign_order stamps assigned_driver_id at OFFER time (189_dispatch_pickup_centered.sql:84) and dispatch_sweep clears+re-stamps it within the same 20s tick (025_auto_dispatch.sql:196-233), so the column is null only for milliseconds — the watchdog samples always see a driver. Proof it misses real incidents: the mig 200 header records an order that pushed the customer every minute 'for over a day' across 3,429 offer laps and was found by a USER report, not the watchdog (200_driver_assigned_notification_loop.sql:5-20). (b) Manual dispatcher offers are inserted with NO offer_expires_at (150_cod_ceiling_enforcement.sql:83); the sweep only expires offers where offer_expires_at is not null (025:199-201), and auto_assign_order bails while any 'offered' row exists (189:29) — so a manual offer to a driver who never responds blocks auto-dispatch forever, with assigned_driver_id set, alerting nobody. (c) status 'preparing' is absent from v_stuck entirely.
impact: The exact failure classes that produced the 2026-07-31 production incident remain invisible to the alerting layer: an order can loop or sit behind a dead manual offer indefinitely while the watchdog reports all-clear. Mig 201 narrows (a) but does not eliminate it (real online drivers who serially decline/lapse keep assigned_driver_id populated), and (b) and (c) are untouched.
fix_sketch: Redefine 'stuck' as: status in ('accepted','preparing','ready') AND no order_assignments row with status='accepted' AND placed_at (or dispatch_eligible_at) older than threshold — independent of assigned_driver_id. Give manual offers a TTL (or a much longer one) so they expire like auto offers; alert separately on orders whose assignment count exceeds N.

title: Assignment lifecycle is not synchronized with order lifecycle: a driver can accept an already-cancelled order, and a manually-displaced driver is never released from on_job
evidence: (1) driver_respond (latest body 030_driver_verified_gate.sql:80-103) locks the assignment row and checks only status='offered' — it never reads orders.status. Admin/dispatcher may cancel from ANY non-terminal state (103_card_delivery_driver_earnings.sql:70-71), and the terminal driver-release (103:88-95) runs at cancel time, i.e. BEFORE the accept. So within the 45s offer TTL a driver can accept a cancelled order: order_assignments becomes 'accepted' permanently, drivers.status is set 'on_job' (030:99) with no future terminal transition to ever release it, and rider_snapshot is re-stamped onto the cancelled order (030:101-103). (2) assign_driver (latest 150_cod_ceiling_enforcement.sql:82-84) marks a prior 'accepted' assignment 'reassigned' but never resets the displaced driver's on_job status; the only on_job→online writer in the codebase is advance_order_status's terminal block, which targets only the CURRENT assigned_driver_id (grep "set status = 'online'" hits only 054/103).
impact: Stranded drivers: in both paths a real driver ends up on_job with no active job, excluded from nearest_drivers (status='online' filter) and thus from all dispatch, until they manually toggle offline/online — the same fleet-erosion failure mig 054 was written to kill, reintroduced via the reassign and accept-after-cancel edges. Case (1) also sends a driver to a restaurant for food that will never be handed over (the mig 093 cancel push mitigates but the DB still allows the accept).
fix_sketch: In driver_respond's accept branch, re-read the order FOR UPDATE and raise unless orders.status in ('accepted','preparing','ready') and assigned_driver_id = v_asg.driver_id. In assign_driver, after marking a prior 'accepted' assignment reassigned, release that driver (update drivers set status='online' where id=old_driver and status='on_job'). Optionally have advance_order_status terminal block also close open 'offered'/'accepted' assignment rows.

title: validate_promo max_uses cap is racy across different users — capped campaign codes can be over-redeemed under concurrency
evidence: validate_promo counts promo_redemptions with no lock on the promo_codes row (058_minted_promo_owner_binding.sql, 'if v_promo.max_uses is not null then select count(*)...'); it is declared STABLE; place_order's only serialization is the PER-USER advisory lock pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended(v_user::text,0)) (153:188), which does not serialize two different users redeeming the same code; the later promo_redemptions insert (153:334-339) has uniqueness only on order_id.
impact: N concurrent checkouts by N distinct users against a max_uses-capped campaign code can each pass the count check and all redeem, exceeding max_uses by up to the concurrency level. Overspend is bounded by max_discount_egp per redemption but is exactly the failure mode a launch-promo spike produces.
fix_sketch: In place_order (not in STABLE validate_promo), take 'select ... from promo_codes where id = ... for update' (or an advisory lock keyed on the promo id) before re-checking counts and inserting the redemption; alternatively enforce with a redemption-count column guarded by a CHECK.

title: place_order has no upper bound on p_tip or cart quantity — absurd-magnitude COD orders pass all validation
evidence: 153_vertical_stage_enforcement.sql:259-260 validates only 'v_qty < 1'; :292-293 and :311 apply only greatest(0, coalesce(p_tip,0)) with no ceiling; schema checks are one-sided (002_app_schema.sql:288 'tip_egp >= 0'; 009_order_items.sql:68 'quantity > 0'). Menu prices got plausibility rails precisely for this reason (132_menu_price_bounds.sql: 'price sits upstream of every money figure'), but tip and quantity did not.
impact: An authenticated (incl. anonymous-auth guest) caller can place a COD order with tip=1,000,000,000 or quantity=100,000, producing near-INT_MAX totals that pollute orders/driver_earnings/driver_cash_ledger, feed the COD-exposure ceiling (migs 149/150 — a delivered absurd order blocks the driver from all further COD dispatch), and skew every revenue/settlement aggregate. True int overflow fails closed with a raw Postgres error, but sub-overflow magnitudes sail through.
fix_sketch: Add plausibility rails mirroring mig 132: e.g. quantity <= 50 per line and tip <= a platform_settings-configurable cap (e.g. 1000 EGP) inside place_order, plus matching one-sided CHECK constraints on orders.tip_egp and order_items.quantity (NOT VALID then VALIDATE).

title: Driver cash-change parser accepts unbounded tender: a self-consistent marker injected via direct place_order call can instruct the driver to prepare arbitrary change
evidence: apps/driver/src/cashChangeNote.ts:49-68 validates a marker only by integer-ness, changeEgp < tenderEgp, and reconciliation `changeEgp === tenderEgp - Math.ceil(collectibleEgp)`; there is no upper bound on tenderEgp. The writer bounds tender to total + 5 largest notes (apps/customer/src/lib/cashChange.ts:15-27,46: maxPlausibleTender = payable + 200*5), but only inside the customer app. orders.dropoff_note is free text supplied to place_order, so a caller bypassing the app (curl/PostgREST) can plant `[[sharmeats:cash-change:v1:tender=100000;change=<100000-total>]]` which reconciles and is rendered as an authoritative instruction via DropoffPreferenceCard (apps/driver/app/job/[id].tsx:402 passes collectibleEgp={job.total_egp}). Neither cashChangeNote.ts nor cashChangeNote.test.ts contains any plausibility bound (grep for bound/LARGEST returns nothing).
impact: Bounded but real doorstep social-engineering aid: the driver app itself tells the driver 'customer pays 100,000 — hand back 99,428' on a 572 EGP order, lending app authority to a quick-change scam. No direct money movement (the driver must physically receive the tender first), which is why this is P2 not P0; but commit da8e3ba explicitly set out to close the injected-marker class and left this residual.
fix_sketch: Mirror the writer's bound in the reader: reject (degrade to visible plain text) any marker where tenderEgp > Math.ceil(collectibleEgp) + 1000 (share the LARGEST_NOTE_EGP * MAX_CHANGE_NOTES constant, documented as mirrored like delivery_proof_required is). Add a regression test with an oversized-but-reconciling marker.

title: New Arabic driver/restaurant locales (2026-07-30) never sync to users.locale, so all server pushes to AR-selecting drivers and merchant staff arrive in English
evidence: expo-push localizes per recipient from public.users.locale (supabase/functions/expo-push/index.ts:263-276, copy.ts:200-207). The customer app writes locale to the server (apps/customer/src/data/supabase/user.ts:50), but the driver app persists its EN/AR choice only to AsyncStorage (apps/driver/src/i18n-context.tsx:60-68, DRIVER_LOCALE_STORAGE_KEY) and the restaurant app likewise has no users.locale write — grep across apps/driver and apps/restaurant finds no update/upsert of users.locale or any locale RPC. AR locales landed 2026-07-30: commits 0015815 'feat(driver): add Arabic core shift localization' and bd9d8ee 'feat(restaurant): add Arabic operational locale' (after the 07-24 audit).
impact: An Arabic-first driver who switches the app to Arabic still receives new_offer, order_ready_pickup, order_cancelled_driver, settlement and KYC pushes in English; same for merchant staff (order_placed_merchant, low_rating, settlement_*). The copy exists — copy.ts has complete AR strings for every event — it is only the per-user locale signal that is missing for these two surfaces, so the 'right party in their language' guarantee holds for customers but not for the supply side the AR work targeted.
fix_sketch: In both apps' setLocale (i18n-context), fire a best-effort server write alongside AsyncStorage: update public.users set locale = <choice> for auth.uid() (column-grant permitting; else a tiny set_my_locale RPC). Also backfill on app start when the stored choice differs from the server value.

title: Driver settlements never notify the driver — settlement pushes exist only for restaurants
evidence: notify_settlement_change and its trigger are bound only to restaurant_settlements (supabase/migrations/093_n7_notification_coverage_gaps.sql:76-121, trigger at 115-118: 'restaurant_settlements_notify_change'). driver_settlements (105_payout_details_and_driver_settlements.sql) contains no notify/push/http_post at all, and grep across all migrations shows no other trigger or sender referencing driver_settlements notifications. settlement_paid/settlement_finalized copy exists in all 5 locales (copy.ts) and both events are ESSENTIAL_EVENTS (prefs.ts:48-49) — the transport and copy exist, the driver-side producer does not.
impact: Drivers — who carry COD cash and are settled weekly by cron (sharmeats-weekly-driver-settlement, mig 105) — get no push when their settlement is finalized or when their payout is marked paid, while restaurants do. 'Money moved' events reach one supply side only; drivers discover payouts only by opening the app, which invites cash-reconciliation disputes.
fix_sketch: Add an AFTER UPDATE OF status trigger on driver_settlements mirroring notify_settlement_change: resolve drivers.profile_id, send settlement_finalized/settlement_paid with recipientUserIds=[profile_id] and an explicit route to the driver earnings screen.

title: Settlement pushes smuggle the settlement UUID into orderId, so a tap deep-links merchant staff to /order/<settlement-id>
evidence: supabase/migrations/093_n7_notification_coverage_gaps.sql:101-106: jsonb_build_object('event', v_event, 'orderId', new.id::text, ...) where new.id is the restaurant_settlements row id (comment admits: 'settlement id; expo-push requires the field'). The expo-push contract was fixed 2026-07-27 to make orderId optional precisely because of this category error (supabase/functions/expo-push/index.ts:115-128: 'Senders with no order to point at smuggled another id into the field... so taps landed on /order/<not-an-order-of-mine>'), and a route field now exists — but this sender was never migrated. Support-chat pushes have the same shape (070_support_chat_push.sql:55-62, orderId = user_id) though clients route those on event.
impact: A merchant staffer tapping 'Weekly statement ready' / 'Payout sent' is routed via orderId to an order screen for a UUID that is not an order — a dead-end error screen at exactly the money moment. Low frequency (weekly) but a paid-flow tap that always breaks.
fix_sketch: New migration: rebuild notify_settlement_change from the deployed body (pg_get_functiondef pattern of migs 164/165) dropping orderId and passing route => the merchant settlements screen; same sweep for any other sender still stuffing non-order ids into orderId.

title: The push-receipts cron exists only out-of-band: no migration schedules push_receipt_sweep, so a rebuilt/staging database silently loses receipt polling
evidence: 174_push_receipt_sweep.sql defines public.push_receipt_sweep() but contains no cron.schedule; the full cron.schedule inventory across supabase/migrations/*.sql (checked) schedules every other sweep (dispatch, auto-accept, settlement, fx, site-health...) but never push_receipt_sweep. Production runs it anyway — docs/OPS-RUNBOOK.md:388 documents cron 'sharmeats-push-receipts, every 15 min', matching the verified live-prod fact 'push-receipts @15m' — so the job was created in the dashboard, not in a migration.
impact: Violates the repo's own reproducibility rule (migrations are the source of truth; H-01 in the 07-24 audit was exactly migration/prod divergence). A DR restore, staging build, or the isolated-Postgres migration suite yields a database where DeviceNotRegistered pruning, provider_accepted settlement, retryable receipt marking, and the project-wide-credential-failure ops_alert (expo-push-receipts/index.ts:210-218) all silently never run.
fix_sketch: One-line migration: select cron.schedule('sharmeats-push-receipts', '*/15 * * * *', $$select public.push_receipt_sweep();$$); — cron.schedule upserts by name (mig 114 pattern) so applying over the existing prod job is a no-op.

title: Push retry pipeline (Package 03 Slice D) has no runner: claim_push_retries / settle_push_attempt are never invoked, so retryable_failed attempts are recorded and then abandoned
evidence: claim_push_retries and settle_push_attempt are defined in 173_push_retry_claim.sql but repo-wide grep finds no caller anywhere (only db-types). No cron.schedule references them (full cron list across supabase/migrations), and no edge function calls them — expo-push/index.ts:344-354 marks 429/5xx/network chunk failures 'retryable_failed' with next_attempt_at, and expo-push-receipts/index.ts:171-177 sets next_attempt_at with the comment 'The dispatcher picks this up; first backoff is one minute' — but no dispatcher exists. Commit 73e28df (2026-07-30) says 'retry dispatcher and receipt poller (mig 173 applied, Slices D+E)': only the SQL claim function was applied, not any consumer.
impact: The headline promise of the outbox package — 'a batch lost to a 429 or 5xx is no longer lost silently and permanently' (171_push_outbox.sql:15-20) — is not fulfilled: on any transient Expo outage, first-attempt failures are durably recorded and then never retried, expiring quietly. Bounded (only failed first attempts are affected; normal sends work), but it is exactly the silent-loss mode the tables were built to close, and the commit history says it is done.
fix_sketch: Add a small dispatcher edge function (or extend expo-push with an internal 'retry' mode) that calls claim_push_retries(100), re-sends each claimed attempt in the recipient's locale, and settles via settle_push_attempt; schedule it with pg_cron every 1-2 minutes using the push_headers() vault pattern of mig 174. This same component can consume fresh queued messages, closing finding 1 simultaneously.

title: Mig 200 rebuilt notify_order_transition from mig 073's body, silently discarding mig 165's dynamically-applied vertical patch — and its stated house-rule-2 verification is factually wrong
evidence: 200_driver_assigned_notification_loop.sql:42-45 claims 'body started from mig 073, the only existing definition, verified via grep -l ... returning exactly one file'. But 165_push_vertical_context.sql:41-84 redefines notify_order_transition in production via pg_get_functiondef + replace() (adding 'vertical', new.vertical_id to every payload) — a definition grep -l for 'function public.notify_order_transition' cannot see. Mig 200's new body also passes no p_vertical to any of its three enqueue_push calls (200:61-95), so the queued rows carry vertical NULL.
impact: User-facing impact today is ~nil: expo-push falls back to resolving orders.vertical_id itself (index.ts:224-238), and the three events currently never send anyway (finding 1). But the prod function body and the repo's replay now diverge from what mig 165's verify block asserts (prosrc must contain 'vertical' — a fresh migration replay of 165 then 200 leaves notify_order_transition WITHOUT it, while 165's check ran before 200), and the repo's own house-rule verification recipe (grep -l) is demonstrated insufficient against dynamic-SQL redefinitions — the exact 'silently reverts later hardening' hazard rule 2 exists to prevent.
fix_sketch: Follow-up migration: re-add p_vertical => new.vertical_id to the three enqueue_push calls in notify_order_transition, and amend the migration-house-rules doc to require checking pg_get_functiondef-based patch migrations (grep for the function NAME, not just 'function public.<name>') when establishing the latest body.

title: Late settlement of a locally-cancelled card order writes a status-event 'placed' and sends an order_paid push while orders.status='cancelled'
evidence: supabase/functions/paymob-webhook/index.ts:169-178: on settled.transitioned it unconditionally inserts order_status_events(status='placed', note 'Payment confirmed (card)') and pushes event 'order_paid'. settle_paymob_payment (mig 180:312-318) deliberately transitions payment_status 'failed'->'paid' after reconcile_stale_card_orders has already set status='cancelled' (033:186-201) — the by-design case mig 181 class h detects (181:209-227) — but the webhook does not distinguish it.
impact: The immutable order_status_events trail shows 'placed' occurring after 'cancelled' (corrupting the audit timeline the state machine otherwise guarantees), and the customer receives an 'order paid' notification for an order that is cancelled and actually needs a refund. Money exposure is bounded (class h daily alert), the messaging/audit trail is not.
fix_sketch: Have settle_paymob_payment return the order's current status; in the webhook, when status is cancelled/rejected skip the 'placed' event and send a 'payment received — order was cancelled, refund incoming' notification (and optionally auto-insert the order_refunds 'requested' claim so class h pressure becomes a queued refund).

title: merchant-web OrderQueue and admin DispatchBoard lack the stale-channel teardown guard — .on('postgres_changes') can throw on remount
evidence: apps/merchant-web/src/app/OrderQueue.tsx:61-63 and apps/admin-web/src/app/DispatchBoard.tsx:60-63 call supabase.channel(name).on('postgres_changes', ...) with no prior getChannels()/removeChannel sweep. Installed @supabase/realtime-js 2.107.0 (both web apps): RealtimeClient.channel() returns the EXISTING channel if one with the same topic is still registered (dist/main/RealtimeClient.js:343-354), removeChannel only splices the list after the async unsubscribe completes (RealtimeClient.js:270-276, _remove at 437), and RealtimeChannel.js:409 throws "cannot add `postgres_changes` callbacks for ... after `subscribe()`". All five Expo-side subscribers guard exactly this (e.g. apps/customer/src/data/supabase/orders.ts:280-288 documents the failure verbatim); the two Next.js dashboards do not.
impact: On a fast unmount/remount of the component (client-side nav away and back, or React StrictMode's double-effect in dev) while the previous removeChannel is still in flight, the effect receives the already-subscribed channel and .on() throws inside the effect — unhandled, it takes down the order queue / dispatch board to the error boundary, i.e. the kitchen stops seeing orders until reload. Narrow race window in production, hence P2.
fix_sketch: Copy the guard used everywhere else: before .channel(name), iterate supabase.getChannels() and removeChannel any channel whose topic === `realtime:${name}`.

title: Admin support inbox neither subscribes to realtime nor polls — support_messages is published for exactly this and only the customer end is live
evidence: apps/admin-web/src/app/support/page.tsx:106-127 — loadThreads() runs once on mount; the file contains no .channel()/postgres_changes and no setInterval (grep confirms). Migration 069_support_chat.sql:132-139 added support_messages to supabase_realtime (replica identity full) and its comment says "Realtime-published" for live delivery; the customer app subscribes live (apps/customer/src/data/supabase/support.ts:52-76, apps/customer/src/hooks/useUnreadBadges.ts:72-76).
impact: An ops agent sitting on the support inbox never sees a new customer message (or a new thread) until they manually re-open a thread or reload the page — the "live support chat" is live in one direction only. Bounded: it is an internal surface and the docs/PLATFORM-GAPS.md ops-support section already defers broader support-console work (order lookup / customer 360), but that deferred item does not cover the inbox being static, and the publication entry that fixes it already exists.
fix_sketch: Add a postgres_changes INSERT subscription on support_messages (admin RLS policy in mig 069 already grants read-all) that calls loadThreads() and, when the inserted row's user_id === openUser, re-runs openThread; include the SUBSCRIBED-resync pattern used elsewhere. A 30s poll fallback would also do.

title: my_kyc_documents is SECURITY DEFINER over the KYC table and was never revoked from PUBLIC/anon — house rule 3 violation; it fails closed today only by accident of NULL semantics
evidence: supabase/migrations/075_kyc_and_vat.sql:123-138 defines `public.my_kyc_documents(kyc_subject_type, uuid)` as `security definer` returning `setof public.kyc_documents`, then issues only `grant execute … to authenticated` (line 138) with no preceding `revoke all … from public, anon`. Granting to authenticated does not remove the default PUBLIC EXECUTE (CLAUDE.md house rule 3), so anon holds it. No later migration revokes it (`grep -n "my_kyc" supabase/migrations/*.sql` shows 075 only). It is one of the advisor's 30 anon-executable definer functions. It happens not to leak because its WHERE has `d.profile_id = auth.uid()` (NULL for anon), `public.is_merchant_staff(...)` (false), and `public.auth_role() = 'admin'` — which for anon evaluates to NULL, filtering the row out rather than passing it.
impact: No data leak at HEAD. The exposure is structural: the third disjunct is the fail-open shape house rule 4 exists to ban (`role = 'admin'` rather than `coalesce(role,'') = 'admin'`), and this function returns whole `kyc_documents` rows — national ID, driving licence, commercial registration and tax-card metadata. Any future edit that adds an unguarded OR branch, or a Postgres/PostgREST change in how a role-less call resolves, turns an anon-callable function into a KYC dump. Same pattern (definer + grant-without-revoke) also affects recent_push_campaigns (078:141-152) and my_restaurant_settlements (074:169-180), which fail closed for the same NULL reason.
fix_sketch: Add `revoke all on function public.my_kyc_documents(kyc_subject_type, uuid) from public, anon;` (and the same for recent_push_campaigns(int) and my_restaurant_settlements(int)) in a new migration, and rewrite the admin disjuncts to `coalesce(public.auth_role()::text,'') = 'admin'`. Then add a CI assertion over pg_proc × pg_default_acl that no `prosecdef` function in public retains EXECUTE for anon/PUBLIC outside a small documented allowlist (search_catalog, can_view_vertical, vertical_effective_stage, current_fx_rates, get_shared_order, my_favorite_items).

title: The 5 advisor-flagged mutable-search_path functions are all SECURITY INVOKER — advisor noise, not an escalation path, but the class needs a lint so a future SECURITY DEFINER edit is caught
evidence: All five defining sites confirmed to lack `SET search_path` AND to lack `security definer`: public.delivery_job_events_immutable — supabase/migrations/193_delivery_job_model.sql:213-217 (`returns trigger language plpgsql as $$ … raise exception … $$`, no definer); private.delivery_access_events_immutable — 191_delivery_dark_config.sql:114-118; public.availability_events_immutable — 188_c0_catalog_foundations.sql:108-114; public.menu_items_staff_writable_columns — 136_merchant_staff_role_enforcement.sql:453-464 (`language sql immutable`, body is a bare `select array['is_available','sort_order']`, references no schema-qualified object); public.search_catalog — 188_c0_catalog_foundations.sql:126-166 (`language sql stable`, deliberately SECURITY INVOKER per the comment at 122-125, and every table reference is schema-qualified `public.menu_items` / `public.restaurants`). Contrast with the surrounding definer functions, all of which DO pin: 188:62, 191:135/183/241, 193:30/47/293/364/467.
impact: Not exploitable. A SECURITY INVOKER function runs with the caller's own privileges, so a hijacked search_path buys the attacker nothing they did not already have; three of the five are trigger bodies whose entire content is `raise exception`, and one returns a literal array. The cost is that these five permanently occupy the advisor's function_search_path_mutable warning list, which is exactly the "advisor noise makes real regressions harder to detect" problem M-06 of docs/AUDIT-REPORT-2026-07-24.md already called out — a future migration that adds `security definer` to any of them (menu_items_staff_writable_columns is the plausible one, since it is read by the definer guard menu_items_guard_privileged_columns) would produce a genuine hijack surface and would not stand out.
fix_sketch: Add `set search_path = pg_catalog, public, pg_temp` (or `= pg_catalog` for the two literal-only ones) to all five so the advisor list goes to zero, then add a migration-time assertion that every `prosecdef` function in public/private has a non-null proconfig search_path — turning the advisor's signal into a hard gate instead of a list someone has to remember is benign.

title: create_delivery_job's in-transaction stage re-check fails OPEN when the service-area config row is missing
evidence: supabase/migrations/193_delivery_job_model.sql:403-407: `select * into v_cfg from delivery_service_configs where service_area_id = v_quote.service_area_id; if v_cfg.launch_stage = 'disabled' or v_cfg.intake_state <> 'open' then raise DELIVERY_NOT_AVAILABLE`. Contrast 192_delivery_pricing_quotes.sql:143-147, which correctly guards `v_cfg.service_area_id is null` first in the quote path.
impact: Bounded: reaching it requires a valid unconsumed quote (mig 192 fails closed, so a config row existed at quote time) plus deletion of the config row inside the quote TTL (service_role-only writes, 191:43-44). But the re-check exists precisely for 'config changed after quoting' (comment 193:402: 'a quote is not a promise'), and the delete case bypasses it — a house-rule-4 violation in the delivery authority path.

title: settle_paymob_payment compares nullable orders.paymob_txn_id with `<>` — a paid order with NULL txn id treats a different transaction as a benign duplicate instead of raising
evidence: supabase/migrations/180_payment_integrity_reapply.sql:306-311: inside the `payment_status='paid'` branch, `if v_order.paymob_txn_id <> btrim(p_provider_txn_id) then raise ORDER_ALREADY_PAID_BY_ANOTHER_TRANSACTION`. If paymob_txn_id is NULL (paid via a legacy path that set only payment_status, e.g. 011_rpcs.sql:463-style updates), the comparison is NULL, the incident raise is skipped, and the function proceeds to mark the payment_attempt 'paid' (:322-327) and return transitioned=false. The same migration uses the safe form elsewhere (`is distinct from` at :193).
impact: Bounded and currently dormant (card payments dark, function service_role-only, and webhook-settled orders normally carry txn ids), but it downgrades the double-payment incident signal — a second, different provider transaction against an already-paid order would be swallowed as a duplicate no-op instead of raising, exactly the reconciliation alarm this function exists to fire. Must be fixed before the card flag flips.
fix_sketch: Use `if v_order.paymob_txn_id is distinct from btrim(p_provider_txn_id) then raise ...` so a NULL stored txn id on a paid order raises (fail closed) rather than silently no-ops.

title: Five private-schema tables created in migs 191-193 omit the house-rule-5b revoke-before-grant
evidence: No `revoke all on table ...` exists for: private.delivery_access_events (191_delivery_dark_config.sql:104), private.delivery_quotes (192_delivery_pricing_quotes.sql:71), private.delivery_job_endpoints (193_delivery_job_model.sql:157), private.delivery_job_parcel_details (193:173), private.delivery_job_transitions (193:225). Mitigations: schema USAGE on `private` is revoked from public/anon/authenticated (152:197) and the documented default ACL is scoped to `in schema public` (141:78, 168:102-104), so no current client-reachable path exists.
impact: Hygiene drift, not an active hole: two independent layers (no schema USAGE, PostgREST does not expose `private`) currently protect these tables — including PII ciphertext (delivery_job_endpoints) and the state-machine table (delivery_job_transitions, whose corruption would alter delivery authority). But the codebase's own rule exists because layered assumptions have failed here before (mig 180's PUBLIC-grant correction of mig 121); a future `grant usage on schema private` for a helper role would silently expose whatever default/implicit grants exist.
fix_sketch: One migration: `revoke all on table private.delivery_access_events, private.delivery_quotes, private.delivery_job_endpoints, private.delivery_job_parcel_details, private.delivery_job_transitions from public, anon, authenticated;` (or `revoke all on all tables in schema private ...` re-run, as 152:244 did).

title: settle_paymob_payment: NULL-unsafe '<>' comparison on orders.paymob_txn_id lets a second transaction against an already-paid card order skip the incident raise
evidence: supabase/migrations/180_payment_integrity_reapply.sql:308 — `if v_order.paymob_txn_id <> btrim(p_provider_txn_id) then raise 'ORDER_ALREADY_PAID_BY_ANOTHER_TRANSACTION'`. orders.paymob_txn_id is nullable; if an order ever reaches payment_status='paid' with a NULL paymob_txn_id (manual ops fix-up, legacy path), the comparison evaluates NULL, the exception is skipped, and execution falls through to mark the payment_attempt 'paid' (line 324-329) while returning transitioned=false. impact: Bounded: no money moves and order state is not overwritten (the orders UPDATE only runs in the pending/failed branch), but a duplicate/mismatched provider transaction that should page as an incident is silently swallowed and the attempt row is stamped paid with the new txn id. Card payments are currently dark, so this is a pre-enable hardening item, not an active path.
fix_sketch: Change line 308 to `if v_order.paymob_txn_id is distinct from btrim(p_provider_txn_id) then raise ...` in a new migration that re-issues only this function (latest body is 180's — house rule 2), before EXPO_PUBLIC_PAYMENTS_CARD_ENABLED is flipped.

title: Mig 200 dedupe keys 'driver_assigned' to the first OFFER, so the customer is told a driver is coming when none accepted — and is never told when one actually does
evidence: supabase/migrations/200_driver_assigned_notification_loop.sql:60-66 — notify_order_transition fires driver_assigned on old.assigned_driver_id null→not-null, which auto_assign_order performs at OFFER creation (189:84), before driver_respond acceptance; idempotency key 'driver_assigned:<order_id>' means exactly one send per order, consumed by that first offer. Offer expiry then nulls assigned_driver_id (dispatch_sweep step 1, 033) and later re-offers/acceptances can never notify (key already taken).
impact: Bounded misinformation in a paid flow: if the first offered driver rejects or times out, the customer has been pushed 'a driver is heading to the restaurant' that was never true, and gets no push when the real driver accepts minutes later. The 2026-07-31 spam loop is genuinely fixed (verified: enqueue_push ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on the unique key, 172_enqueue_push.sql:114; no migration ever deletes push_messages rows so the key cannot be recycled), but the fix froze the wrong semantic moment.
fix_sketch: Move the customer-facing driver_assigned enqueue from the orders trigger to driver_respond's accept branch (the moment it becomes true), keeping the same 'driver_assigned:<order_id>' key so it stays once-per-order; or key on assignment status transition offered→accepted.

title: An offer a live driver never saw counts as a 1-hour 'rejected' cooldown against that order, so one busy moment can starve an order of its whole nearby fleet
evidence: dispatch_sweep marks TTL-lapsed offers status='rejected' (033_card_payment_guards.sql dispatch_sweep step 1); auto_assign_order then excludes any driver with a rejected/reassigned assignment newer than dispatch_reoffer_cooldown_seconds (default 3600) for that order (189:55-56). A 45s unanswered push — phone in pocket at a red light — is indistinguishable from an explicit decline. Mig 201's header documents the pathological form (every driver cooled down, order paused an hour) but 201 only removed dead phones from the pool; live drivers who miss one offer still burn the full hour.
impact: With Sharm's small launch fleet, an order placed at a rush moment can exhaust its 3-5 nearby drivers in ~4 minutes of offer cycles and then receive no offers for up to an hour, surfacing only via the dispatch_watchdog page (10-min threshold, 60-min alert cooldown per migs 119/133). Bounded and human-recoverable, hence P2, but it converts a missed push into an hour-long per-order lockout.
fix_sketch: Distinguish explicit rejection from expiry: mark lapsed offers 'expired' (new enum value) and give them a much shorter re-offer cooldown (e.g. 120-300s) than explicit rejections, or shrink the cooldown automatically when the candidate pool for an order is exhausted.

title: auto_advance 'preparing' timer keys on updated_at, which dispatch offer-churn refreshes — deferring preparing→ready exactly while the order is also invisible to the watchdog
evidence: auto_advance_sweep uses coalesce(o.updated_at,...) as the state-entry time for 'preparing' (039_auto_advance_kitchen.sql:74-92). orders_touch_updated_at is an unconditional BEFORE UPDATE trigger on orders (002_app_schema.sql:354-355), and the dispatch loop writes the order row at least twice per ~65s cycle (offer stamp 189:84; expiry clear 025:204-208), so a 'preparing' order under active offer churn never accumulates the 240s idle window and never advances to 'ready'. Meanwhile 'preparing' is excluded from the watchdog's v_stuck (133_watchdog_placed_orders.sql).
impact: Bounded but real stall: while online drivers serially lapse offers, the order neither progresses to 'ready' nor trips any alert; it unsticks only when all candidates enter the 1h reoffer cooldown and churn stops. Adds minutes-to-tens-of-minutes of silent latency in exactly the thin-fleet dinner-rush case.
fix_sketch: Track state entry explicitly (add preparing_at, or derive from the order_status_events row for 'preparing') instead of updated_at; or make orders_touch_updated_at an UPDATE OF (status,...) trigger so assignment churn stops touching it.

title: place_order still accepts p_scheduled_for server-side while every sweep ignores it — the scheduled-orders gate is client-only
evidence: Latest place_order (153_vertical_stage_enforcement.sql:145,306,320) accepts and stores p_scheduled_for with no validation. auto_accept_sweep filters only on placed_at age (026_auto_accept.sql:80-90), dispatch_sweep on status (025:216-228), auto_advance_sweep on accepted_at/updated_at (039:74-92) — none checks scheduled_for. The gate shipped 2026-07-30 is client-side only: apps/customer/src/lib/scheduledOrders.ts:13-15 + apps/customer/eas.json:28 (EXPO_PUBLIC_SCHEDULED_ORDERS_ENABLED=false), per docs/agent-handoffs/2026-07-30-codex-scheduled-order-gate.md, which itself notes the backend lifecycle does not exist yet.
impact: Any authenticated user calling the RPC directly (place_order is client-callable) can create an order with a future scheduled_for that is auto-accepted in 3 min, cooked, and dispatched immediately — food made ~a day early, COD driver dispatched for a customer expecting tomorrow. Exposure is limited to hand-crafted API calls (the shipped app cannot send it), and the feature-dark decision is documented, so this is hardening rather than a live break.
fix_sketch: Until the delayed-release lifecycle exists, have place_order raise on non-null p_scheduled_for (or clamp to null), mirroring the fail-closed client gate at the authority layer; when the feature ships, add `scheduled_for is null or scheduled_for <= now() + prep window` filters to auto_accept/dispatch/auto_advance.

title: Mig 200 residual notification-semantics gaps: 'driver on the way' fires at OFFER time and can never fire again; order_ready_pickup cannot reach a driver assigned after 'ready' despite its per-driver key
evidence: driver_assigned is triggered by assigned_driver_id null→not-null (200_driver_assigned_notification_loop.sql:60-66), which auto_assign_order sets when merely OFFERING (189:84) — so the customer is told a driver is coming before anyone accepted, and the once-per-order key 'driver_assigned:<order_id>' means if that first offer lapses and a different driver accepts hours later (or manual reassignment occurs), no further customer notification is structurally possible. Separately, the order_ready_pickup branch requires the status transition into 'ready' (200:71-72: old.status is distinct from 'ready'), so its per-(order,driver) idempotency key (200:79) can never produce a second send for a driver who accepts an already-ready order — contradicting the code comment's stated intent ('a re-dispatch to a DIFFERENT driver should reach that driver'); such drivers rely solely on the new_offer push.
impact: Bounded UX/notification correctness: customers can receive a premature 'driver on the way' that is never corrected or repeated even on genuine reassignment; a driver taking over an already-ready order gets no pickup nudge. No money impact; the mig 200 loop fix itself is sound and durable (push_messages.idempotency_key unique, 171_push_outbox.sql:80; no migration ever deletes push_messages rows).
fix_sketch: Fire driver_assigned from driver_respond's accept path (or key it per accepted assignment id) instead of the offer-time column transition; move the order_ready_pickup send to also fire on assigned_driver_id change while status='ready', letting the existing per-(order,driver) key dedupe.
